board_events.text: Answer: A–2, B–4, C–1, D–3.
NEET assertion-reason. A: The release of GM crops requires regulatory approval. R: Genetically modified organisms can have unpredictable effects when introduced into ecosystems.
Answer: (a) — both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

Why R explains A: because GMOs may behave unpredictably in the environment, a body like GEAC must assess their safety before release. The unpredictability is not a side note — it is the entire reason the approval step exists.

segments.text: Two formats, and this match is the one the whole subtopic has been preparing you for. Four items: a regulator, a right, a wrong, and a study.
Column one: G E A C; biopatent; biopiracy; and bioethics.
Column two: unauthorised, uncompensated use of bioresources; approves validity and safety of G M organisms; study of moral issues in biology; and right granted over a biological invention.

Now use the keyword rule instead of your memory. Each option in column two contains its own giveaway word. Approves — that is the regulator. Right granted — that is the patent. Unauthorised — that is the piracy. Study — that is the ethics.
The answer is A two, B four, C one, D three. And notice you did not have to recall a single definition. You matched keywords to terms, and the grid solved itself.
Now the assertion reason. Assertion: the release of G M crops requires regulatory approval. Reason: genetically modified organisms can have unpredictable effects when introduced into ecosystems.
The answer is option a. Both are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

And the link here is as tight as any in the chapter. Because G M Os may behave unpredictably in the environment, a body like G E A C must assess their safety before release. The unpredictability is not a side note sitting next to the rule. It is the entire reason the approval step exists at all. Remove the unpredictability and you would not need the committee.
दो formats, और यह match वही है जिसके लिए पूरा subtopic आपको तैयार कर रहा था। चार items: एक regulator, एक right, एक wrong, और एक study.
Column one: G E A C; biopatent; biopiracy; और bioethics.
Column two: bioresources का अनधिकृत, बिना मुआवज़े का इस्तेमाल; G M organisms की validity और safety को मंज़ूरी देना; biology में नैतिक मुद्दों का अध्ययन; और किसी जैविक आविष्कार पर दिया गया अधिकार।

अब याददाश्त के बजाय keyword rule इस्तेमाल कीजिए। Column two का हर option अपना भेद ख़ुद खोल देता है। Approves — वह regulator है। Right granted — वह patent है। Unauthorised — वह piracy है। Study — वह ethics है।
जवाब है A two, B four, C one, D three. और ग़ौर कीजिए आपको एक भी definition याद नहीं करनी पड़ी। आपने keywords को terms से मिलाया, और grid ख़ुद हल हो गया।
अब assertion reason. Assertion: G M crops छोड़ने के लिए regulatory approval चाहिए। Reason: genetically modified organisms को ecosystems में डालने पर उनके अप्रत्याशित असर हो सकते हैं।
जवाब है option a. दोनों सही हैं, और R, A की सही explanation है।

और यहाँ का link chapter के किसी भी link जितना कसा हुआ है। चूँकि G M O पर्यावरण में अप्रत्याशित व्यवहार कर सकते हैं, इसलिए G E A C जैसी संस्था को छोड़ने से पहले उनकी safety जाँचनी ही होगी। अप्रत्याशितता कोई किनारे बैठा नोट नहीं है। वही पूरी वजह है कि approval वाला क़दम मौजूद ही है। अप्रत्याशितता हटा दीजिए और committee की ज़रूरत ही नहीं बचेगी।

board_events.text: (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct — the exact expansion, two of the three Indian cases, and the reason GEAC exists.
(ii) is the trap — it defines a BIOPATENT, not biopiracy. Biopiracy is the unauthorised, uncompensated use of bioresources.
Notice how the trap is built: statement (ii) is not nonsense. It is a perfectly correct definition — attached to the wrong word.
Answer: (a) — (i), (iii) and (iv).

segments.text: The high difficulty question, and the trap is the most elegant one in the chapter. Nothing in it is false in isolation — the falsehood is in the labelling.
The question. Choose the correct statements.
Statement one: G E A C stands for Genetic Engineering Approval Committee. Statement two: biopiracy is the patent right legally granted over a biological invention.
Statement three: Turmeric and Neem are examples of Indian resources targeted by biopiracy. Statement four: G M Os may have unpredictable effects on ecosystems.
Work the grid. Three greens and one red, and look closely at the red one before you dismiss it.
Statements one, three and four are correct. The exact expansion. Two of the three Indian cases. And the reason G E A C exists in the first place.
Statement two is the trap. It defines a biopatent, not biopiracy. Biopiracy is the unauthorised, uncompensated use of bioresources.

<excited>And see how beautifully the trap is built. Statement two is not nonsense. It is not a garbled sentence or an invented fact. It is a perfectly correct definition — attached to the wrong word. The examiner took a true statement about biopatents and simply changed the label at the front.

So the answer is option a — statements one, three and four. And this is exactly why the mnemonic earns its keep. Patent equals right, piracy equals theft. Statement two says right. Therefore statement two is about the patent, whatever word it starts with.
High difficulty question, और इसका trap chapter का सबसे सुंदर trap है। इसमें अकेले में कुछ भी झूठ नहीं है — झूठ label लगाने में है।
Question. सही statements चुनिए।
Statement one: G E A C का मतलब है Genetic Engineering Approval Committee. Statement two: biopiracy किसी जैविक आविष्कार पर क़ानूनी तौर पर दिया गया patent अधिकार है।
Statement three: Turmeric और Neem ऐसे भारतीय संसाधनों के उदाहरण हैं जो biopiracy का निशाना बने। Statement four: G M O का ecosystems पर अप्रत्याशित असर हो सकता है।
Grid पर काम कीजिए। तीन हरे और एक लाल, और उस लाल वाले को ख़ारिज करने से पहले ग़ौर से देखिए।
Statement one, three और four सही हैं। सटीक expansion. तीन में से दो भारतीय मामले। और वह वजह जिससे G E A C का वजूद ही है।
Statement two trap है। यह biopatent को define करता है, biopiracy को नहीं। Biopiracy है bioresources का अनधिकृत, बिना मुआवज़े का इस्तेमाल।

<excited>और देखिए trap कितनी ख़ूबसूरती से बना है। Statement two बकवास नहीं है। यह न कोई उलझा वाक्य है, न गढ़ा हुआ fact. यह एक बिल्कुल सही definition है — बस ग़लत शब्द से जोड़ दी गई। Examiner ने biopatent के बारे में एक सच्चा बयान लिया और आगे का label भर बदल दिया।

तो जवाब है option a — statements one, three और four. और ठीक इसीलिए वह mnemonic अपनी क़ीमत वसूल करता है। Patent equals right, piracy equals theft. Statement two कहता है right. इसलिए statement two patent के बारे में है, चाहे वह किसी भी शब्द से शुरू होता हो।

sections.title: The keyword rule — and why these are free marks

board_events.text: Four pitfalls in ethics, biopiracy and GEAC
Pitfall 1 — confusing the three 'bio-' terms. Biopatent = right granted. Biopiracy = unauthorised use. Bioethics = the study. Examiners swap these in distractors constantly.
Pitfall 2 — the wrong GEAC expansion. It is Genetic Engineering Approval Committee. Learn it exactly.
Pitfall 3 — mixing up the Indian examples. Turmeric → wound-healing. Neem → fungicidal/medicinal. Basmati → rice variety.
Pitfall 4 — 'biopiracy is legal/fair.' By definition it is the opposite: it lacks authorisation AND compensation.

board_events.text: Pro-Tip — the keyword rule. 'Without authorisation/compensation' → BIOPIRACY. 'Right granted' → BIOPATENT. 'GM safety/approval' → GEAC.
Match the keyword to the term and these questions become free marks — you are recognising a phrase, not recalling a definition.
Mnemonics: 'Patent = right, Piracy = theft, Ethics = study' · 'GEAC = GM gatekeeper' · 'Basmati–Neem–Turmeric = BNT targets.'

segments.text: Let us close the final subtopic — and the chapter's content — at the leak points. Four pitfalls, and they are unusually easy to defend against.

Pitfall one. Confusing the three bio- terms. Biopatent is the right granted. Biopiracy is the unauthorised use. Bioethics is the study. Examiners swap these in distractors constantly, and it is the single most-tested confusion here.
Pitfall two. The wrong G E A C expansion. It is Genetic Engineering Approval Committee. Learn it exactly, word for word, because the distractors are built to sound almost right.

Pitfall three. Mixing up the Indian examples. Turmeric goes with wound-healing. Neem goes with fungicidal and medicinal. Basmati goes with the rice variety. Three plants, three properties, and they get shuffled.

Pitfall four. Thinking biopiracy is legal or fair. By definition it is the opposite — it lacks authorisation and it lacks compensation. If a statement describes a fair, permitted transaction, it is not describing biopiracy.
Look at the board. The keyword rule sits on top, the four pitfalls below with their corrections. And that top strip is the most valuable thing in this section.

So here is the pro tip, and it is a genuine shortcut. If a definition mentions without authorisation or compensation, the answer is biopiracy. If it says right granted, the answer is biopatent. If it mentions G M safety or approval, the answer is G E A C.

<excited>Match the keyword to the term and these questions become free marks. And notice what has changed: you are no longer recalling a definition under pressure. You are recognising a phrase. That is a much easier thing to do in an exam hall.
Three mnemonics to carry out of this subtopic. Patent equals right, piracy equals theft, ethics equals study. G E A C equals G M gatekeeper. And Basmati, Neem, Turmeric — the B N T targets.
आख़िरी subtopic — और chapter की सामग्री — को leak points पर बंद करते हैं। चार pitfalls, और इनसे बचाव असामान्य रूप से आसान है।

Pitfall one. तीनों bio- terms को गड्डमड्ड करना। Biopatent है दिया गया अधिकार। Biopiracy है अनधिकृत इस्तेमाल। Bioethics है अध्ययन। Examiners इन्हें distractors में लगातार बदलते हैं, और यही यहाँ की सबसे ज़्यादा पूछी जाने वाली उलझन है।
Pitfall two. ग़लत G E A C expansion. यह है Genetic Engineering Approval Committee. इसे बिल्कुल सही सीखिए, शब्द दर शब्द, क्योंकि distractors लगभग सही सुनाई देने के लिए बनाए गए हैं।

Pitfall three. भारतीय उदाहरणों को गड्डमड्ड करना। Turmeric जाता है wound-healing के साथ। Neem जाता है fungicidal और medicinal के साथ। Basmati जाता है चावल की क़िस्म के साथ। तीन पौधे, तीन गुण, और इन्हें फेंट दिया जाता है।

Pitfall four. यह सोचना कि biopiracy वैध या न्यायसंगत है। परिभाषा से ही यह उल्टा है — इसमें न अनुमति होती है, न मुआवज़ा। अगर कोई statement किसी निष्पक्ष, अनुमति-प्राप्त लेन-देन का वर्णन करे, तो वह biopiracy का वर्णन नहीं कर रहा।
Board देखिए। ऊपर keyword rule बैठा है, नीचे चारों pitfalls अपने corrections के साथ। और वह ऊपर वाली पट्टी इस section की सबसे क़ीमती चीज़ है।

तो यह रहा pro tip, और यह असली shortcut है। अगर किसी definition में without authorisation या compensation आए, जवाब है biopiracy. अगर वह कहे right granted, जवाब है biopatent. अगर उसमें G M safety या approval आए, जवाब है G E A C.

<excited>Keyword को term से मिलाइए और ये questions मुफ़्त marks बन जाते हैं। और ग़ौर कीजिए क्या बदला: अब आप दबाव में definition याद नहीं कर रहे। आप एक phrase पहचान रहे हैं। Exam hall में यह कहीं आसान काम है।
इस subtopic से तीन mnemonics साथ ले जाइए। Patent equals right, piracy equals theft, ethics equals study. G E A C equals G M gatekeeper. और Basmati, Neem, Turmeric — यानी B N T targets.

sections.title: The whole chapter on three boards

board_events.text: Biotechnology and its Applications — complete cheat sheet

board_events.caption: Cheat sheet 1 of 3 — Agriculture (Bt cotton, RNAi) and Humulin
board_events.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 720 350" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif">
<text x="360" y="20" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1f2933">CHEAT SHEET 1 of 3 — Agriculture & Humulin</text>
<rect x="16" y="32" width="688" height="150" rx="8" fill="#f0fdf4" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="30" y="52" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#166534">1. AGRICULTURE</text>
<text x="30" y="74" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Bt cotton</tspan> = GM cotton carrying cry gene(s) from <tspan font-style="italic">Bacillus thuringiensis</tspan> (a soil BACTERIUM). Toxin = Cry protein = delta-endotoxin (a PROTEIN).</text>
<text x="30" y="92" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">cry genes:</tspan> cryIAc + cryIIAb → cotton bollworm · cryIAb → corn borer</text>
<rect x="30" y="100" width="330" height="34" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#16a34a"/>
<text x="195" y="121" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#166534">crystal → eaten → ALKALINE → pores → dies</text>
<rect x="370" y="100" width="330" height="34" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#2563eb"/>
<text x="535" y="121" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#2563eb">sense + antisense → dsRNA → mRNA silenced → pest dies</text>
<text x="30" y="150" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Protoxin</tspan> (inactive crystal, harmless in bacterium + plant) → <tspan font-weight="bold">active toxin</tspan> only in the insect's ALKALINE midgut. Specificity = alkaline gut + matching receptor.</text>
<text x="30" y="168" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">RNAi</tspan> vs <tspan font-style="italic">Meloidogyne incognita</tspan> (root-knot nematode, tobacco); Agrobacterium vector. RNAi occurs in ALL eukaryotes. Golden Rice = beta-carotene (nutrition, NOT pest-resistance).</text>
<rect x="16" y="192" width="688" height="150" rx="8" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="30" y="212" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#2563eb">2. HUMULIN</text>
<text x="30" y="234" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Animal insulin failed twice:</tspan> tiny yield (mass slaughter) + foreign-protein allergy. Humulin fixes BOTH: scale and safety.</text>
<text x="30" y="252" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Insulin</tspan> = TWO chains, A + B, linked by disulphide bridges. <tspan font-weight="bold">Proinsulin</tspan> = A + C + B as one chain. C-peptide is in proinsulin ONLY.</text>
<text x="30" y="270" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Main challenge:</tspan> getting insulin ASSEMBLED into a mature form — not making the chains.</text>
<rect x="30" y="280" width="330" height="52" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="195" y="298" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#991b1b">BODY = remove C-peptide</text>
<text x="195" y="314" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">proinsulin folds → bridges form → C-peptide cut away</text>
<text x="195" y="327" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" font-style="italic" fill="#475569">fold and bond FIRST, cut SECOND</text>
<rect x="370" y="280" width="330" height="52" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="535" y="298" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#166534">FACTORY = join two chains</text>
<text x="535" y="314" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">Eli Lilly, 1983, E. coli — A and B made SEPARATELY, then</text>
<text x="535" y="327" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">joined by CREATING disulphide bonds. No proinsulin, no C-peptide.</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: Board 1 — the two production stories. Bt cotton: cry genes from a BACTERIUM make a Cry PROTEIN, harmless as a protoxin crystal until an insect's ALKALINE midgut activates it. RNAi: sense + antisense → dsRNA → the pest's mRNA is silenced. Humulin: A and B chains made SEPARATELY in E. coli and joined by CREATING disulphide bonds — the factory route, not the body's C-peptide route.

board_events.caption: Cheat sheet 2 of 3 — Gene Therapy and Molecular Diagnosis
board_events.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 720 350" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif">
<text x="360" y="20" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1f2933">CHEAT SHEET 2 of 3 — Gene Therapy & Molecular Diagnosis</text>
<rect x="16" y="32" width="688" height="146" rx="8" fill="#f0fdf4" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="30" y="52" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#166534">3. GENE THERAPY</text>
<text x="30" y="74" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Definition:</tspan> methods that CORRECT A GENE DEFECT by delivering a normal functional gene, to compensate for the non-functional one.</text>
<rect x="30" y="84" width="670" height="30" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="365" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#166534">1990, ADA gene DELETED → SCID → lymphocytes cultured → functional cDNA via RETROVIRUS → re-infused (NOT permanent)</text>
<text x="30" y="132" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Why not permanent:</tspan> mature lymphocytes are NOT immortal → periodic re-infusion. A permanent cure needs the gene at an EARLY EMBRYONIC STAGE.</text>
<text x="30" y="150" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Therapy = gene. Replacement = product.</tspan> Enzyme replacement supplies the enzyme — temporary, repeated, expensive, NEVER curative.</text>
<text x="30" y="168" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• Best for SINGLE-GENE disorders (enzymatic, immunodeficiency). Vector for human cells = RETROVIRUS (not Agrobacterium, not E. coli).</text>
<rect x="16" y="188" width="688" height="154" rx="8" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="30" y="208" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#2563eb">4. MOLECULAR DIAGNOSIS</text>
<text x="30" y="230" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Why:</tspan> conventional methods (serum/urine) only detect a pathogen once its concentration is HIGH — by then symptoms have appeared and treatment is harder.</text>
<rect x="30" y="240" width="216" height="60" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="138" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#2563eb">PCR</text>
<text x="138" y="274" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">AMPLIFIES nucleic acid</text>
<text x="138" y="290" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">HIV · cancer mutations · genetic disorders</text>
<rect x="254" y="240" width="216" height="60" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="362" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#16a34a">PROBE + autoradiography</text>
<text x="362" y="274" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">SINGLE-stranded DNA/RNA + radioactive tag</text>
<text x="362" y="290" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" font-weight="bold" fill="#dc2626">mutated clone gives NO spot</text>
<rect x="478" y="240" width="222" height="60" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#d97706" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="589" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#d97706">ELISA</text>
<text x="589" y="274" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">ANTIGEN–ANTIBODY interaction</text>
<text x="589" y="290" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">detects antigens OR antibodies</text>
<rect x="150" y="310" width="420" height="28" rx="6" fill="#fef3c7" stroke="#d97706" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="360" y="329" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#92400e">nucleic acid → PCR / probe · protein → ELISA</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: Board 2 — the two medical stories. Gene therapy in one sentence: 1990, ADA gene DELETED → SCID → lymphocytes cultured → functional cDNA via RETROVIRUS → re-infused, and NOT permanent because mature lymphocytes die. Molecular diagnosis in one rule: nucleic acid → PCR or probe; protein → ELISA.

board_events.caption: Cheat sheet 3 of 3 — Transgenic Animals and Ethics, Biopiracy & GEAC
board_events.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 720 350" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif">
<text x="360" y="20" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1f2933">CHEAT SHEET 3 of 3 — Transgenic Animals & Ethics</text>
<rect x="16" y="32" width="688" height="140" rx="8" fill="#f0fdf4" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="30" y="52" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#166534">5. TRANSGENIC ANIMALS</text>
<text x="30" y="74" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Definition:</tspan> DNA manipulated to POSSESS + EXPRESS a foreign gene. Examples: rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows, fish — and <tspan font-weight="bold">~95% are MICE</tspan>.</text>
<rect x="30" y="84" width="670" height="30" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="365" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#166534">P – D – P – V – T : Physiology/development · Disease models · biological Products · Vaccine safety · Toxicity testing</text>
<text x="30" y="132" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Named pairs:</tspan> ROSIE = first transgenic cow (1997) → milk with human α-lactalbumin (~2.4 g/L). SHEEP → α-1-antitrypsin → treats EMPHYSEMA.</text>
<text x="30" y="150" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• Disease models: cancer, cystic fibrosis, rheumatoid arthritis, Alzheimer's. Vaccine: POLIO on transgenic mice (could replace monkeys).</text>
<text x="30" y="164" font-size="10" fill="#dc2626">• Toxicity animals are made MORE SENSITIVE (not resistant). Selective breeding does NOT make an animal transgenic.</text>
<rect x="16" y="182" width="688" height="160" rx="8" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="30" y="202" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#2563eb">6. ETHICS, BIOPIRACY & GEAC</text>
<text x="30" y="224" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Why ethics:</tspan> GMOs may have unpredictable ecosystem effects; patents over living things raise ownership / fairness issues.</text>
<rect x="30" y="234" width="216" height="52" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="138" y="252" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#2563eb">BIOPATENT</text>
<text x="138" y="268" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">the RIGHT granted over a</text>
<text x="138" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">biological invention</text>
<rect x="254" y="234" width="216" height="52" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#dc2626" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="362" y="252" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#dc2626">BIOPIRACY</text>
<text x="362" y="268" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">use of bioresources WITHOUT</text>
<text x="362" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">authorisation or compensatory payment</text>
<rect x="478" y="234" width="222" height="52" rx="6" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="589" y="252" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#16a34a">BIOETHICS</text>
<text x="589" y="268" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">the STUDY of moral issues</text>
<text x="589" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="9" fill="#1f2933">in the biological sciences</text>
<text x="30" y="304" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">GEAC = Genetic Engineering Approval Committee</tspan> → decides VALIDITY of GM research + SAFETY of releasing GM organisms. Remit is safety, NOT patents.</text>
<text x="30" y="322" font-size="10" fill="#1f2933">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Indian targets:</tspan> Basmati (rice variety) · Neem (fungicidal/medicinal) · Turmeric (wound-healing, US patent). <tspan font-weight="bold">Response: the Indian Patents Bill.</tspan></text>
<text x="30" y="337" font-size="10" fill="#dc2626">• Three faces of biopiracy: intellectual (false novelty) · resource (monopoly control) · economic (market exclusion).</text>
</svg>

board_events.text: Board 3 — the animal and the rules. Transgenic animal: DNA manipulated to POSSESS and EXPRESS a foreign gene; ~95% are mice; five uses as P-D-P-V-T. Ethics: Patent = right, Piracy = theft, Ethics = study; GEAC = the GM gatekeeper; Basmati–Neem–Turmeric are the targets and the Indian Patents Bill is the response.

The mnemonic set, all six subtopics: 'protoxin needs an alkaline gut' · 'body removes C-peptide, factory joins two chains' · 'Therapy = gene, Replacement = product' · 'PCR = Photocopy & Reveal; probe is single, mutant gives no spot' · 'P-D-P-V-T' · 'Patent = right, Piracy = theft, Ethics = study'.
And the six one-word triggers: ALKALINE → Bt · SEPARATELY → humulin · PERMANENT → gene therapy · ANTIGEN-ANTIBODY → ELISA · 95% → mice · WITHOUT AUTHORISATION → biopiracy.

segments.text: That is the chapter. Six subtopics, and everything in them now fits onto three boards. Let us walk them one last time — not to learn anything new, but to see the whole shape at once.
Board one. The two production stories, and both are about making a molecule that a living thing did not previously make.

B t cotton: cry genes from a bacterium make a Cry protein, harmless as a protoxin crystal until an insect's alkaline midgut activates it. R N A i: sense plus antisense gives double-stranded R N A, and the pest's messenger R N A is silenced. And humulin: the A and B chains made separately in E coli, then joined by creating disulphide bonds — the factory route, not the body's C-peptide route.
Board two. The two medical stories, and both are about seeing or fixing something at the molecular level.

Gene therapy in one sentence: nineteen ninety, A D A gene deleted, S C I D, lymphocytes cultured, functional c D N A via retrovirus, re-infused — and not permanent, because mature lymphocytes die. Molecular diagnosis in one rule: nucleic acid goes to P C R or a probe; protein goes to E L I S A.
Board three. The animal, and the rules that govern all of it.

Transgenic animal: D N A manipulated to possess and express a foreign gene; about ninety five percent are mice; five uses as P D P V T. And ethics: patent equals right, piracy equals theft, ethics equals study. G E A C is the G M gatekeeper. Basmati, Neem and Turmeric are the targets, and the Indian Patents Bill is the response.

Here is the full mnemonic set, all six subtopics in one breath. Protoxin needs an alkaline gut. Body removes C-peptide, factory joins two chains. Therapy equals gene, replacement equals product. P C R equals photocopy and reveal, probe is single, mutant gives no spot. P D P V T. Patent equals right, piracy equals theft, ethics equals study.

<excited>And if you take one thing into the hall, take this: six one-word triggers. Alkaline points to B t. Separately points to humulin. Permanent points to gene therapy. Antigen-antibody points to E L I S A. Ninety five percent points to mice. And without authorisation points to biopiracy. Six words, six subtopics. When you see the word, you already know the answer.
यह रहा पूरा chapter. छह subtopics, और उनका सब कुछ अब तीन boards पर आ जाता है। एक आख़िरी बार इन पर चलते हैं — कुछ नया सीखने के लिए नहीं, बल्कि पूरी शक्ल एक साथ देखने के लिए।
Board one. दो production की कहानियाँ, और दोनों उस molecule को बनाने के बारे में हैं जो कोई जीव पहले नहीं बनाता था।

B t cotton: एक bacterium से आए cry genes एक Cry protein बनाते हैं, जो protoxin crystal के रूप में हानिरहित है जब तक किसी कीड़े की alkaline midgut उसे activate न कर दे। R N A i: sense और antisense मिलकर double-stranded R N A देते हैं, और कीड़े का messenger R N A ख़ामोश हो जाता है। और humulin: A और B chains E coli में अलग-अलग बनीं, फिर disulphide bonds बनाकर जोड़ी गईं — factory वाला रास्ता, शरीर वाला C-peptide रास्ता नहीं।
Board two. दो चिकित्सा की कहानियाँ, और दोनों आणविक स्तर पर कुछ देखने या ठीक करने के बारे में हैं।

Gene therapy एक वाक्य में: उन्नीस सौ नब्बे, A D A gene deleted, S C I D, lymphocytes cultured, retrovirus से functional c D N A, re-infused — और permanent नहीं, क्योंकि mature lymphocytes मर जाती हैं। Molecular diagnosis एक नियम में: nucleic acid जाता है P C R या probe के पास; protein जाता है E L I S A के पास।
Board three. जानवर, और वे नियम जो इस सब पर शासन करते हैं।

Transgenic animal: D N A manipulate किया गया ताकि वह foreign gene रखे और express करे; लगभग पंचानवे प्रतिशत mice हैं; पाँच uses यानी P D P V T. और ethics: patent equals right, piracy equals theft, ethics equals study. G E A C है G M gatekeeper. Basmati, Neem और Turmeric निशाने हैं, और Indian Patents Bill जवाब है।

यह रहा पूरा mnemonic set, छहों subtopics एक साँस में। Protoxin needs an alkaline gut. Body removes C-peptide, factory joins two chains. Therapy equals gene, replacement equals product. P C R equals photocopy and reveal, probe is single, mutant gives no spot. P D P V T. Patent equals right, piracy equals theft, ethics equals study.

<excited>और अगर hall में एक ही चीज़ ले जानी हो, तो यह ले जाइए: छह एक-शब्द वाले संकेत। Alkaline इशारा करता है B t की तरफ़। Separately इशारा करता है humulin की तरफ़। Permanent इशारा करता है gene therapy की तरफ़। Antigen-antibody इशारा करता है E L I S A की तरफ़। पंचानवे प्रतिशत इशारा करता है mice की तरफ़। और without authorisation इशारा करता है biopiracy की तरफ़। छह शब्द, छह subtopics. जब आप वह शब्द देखेंगे, आपको जवाब पहले से पता होगा।
